NOT in scope: custom WebSocket protocol or browser UI APIs. Hard dependency: Official MCP stdio adapter. Owned paths: packages/mcp/src/http/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test.

Session authentication, bounds, resume, cancellation, and disconnect behavior fail closed.

IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/http/http-session.test.ts. Session/auth matrix with a call-recording fake SessionPort (validate-only). Cases, each asserting fail-closed + ZERO dispatch calls: missing bearer, malformed bearer, expired verdict, revoked verdict; SWAPPED CROSS-BINDING (adapter-owned, testable nowhere else): valid bearer A presented with an Mcp-Session-Id bound to bearer B's session -> refused (the Mcp-Session-Id<->daemon-session binding is adapter state); ROTATION REVOCATION: after the port reports rotation, the OLD bearer fails on the very next request while the Mcp-Session-Id binding survives under the new credential — requires per-request revalidation with NO caching of auth verdicts (assert the port is called every request); CREDENTIAL-IN-URL refusal: any request with a credential-looking query parameter is refused before processing (design 1139 'Credentials never appear in URLs or logs'); redaction: no error path echoes the bearer (grep-style assertion over serialized error bytes). Session lifecycle: initialize binds a daemon session via the port INSIDE the awaited onsessioninitialized callback; DELETE reaps the registry entry and calls port session-close notification; unknown Mcp-Session-Id -> 404 (SDK) with zero dispatch. Confirm RED.

implementationPlan.description: Green — src/http/http-session.ts (target <=250). SessionPort type is VALIDATE-ONLY: { validateBearer(credential): frozen verdict {ok, principalRef, sessionRef} | {ok:false, code}; bindSession(mcpSessionId, verdict): void|Promise; closeSession(mcpSessionId): void|Promise } — deliberately NO open/renew/rotate methods: the daemon owns session lifecycle (session.open|rotate|renew|close commands, design 987/761); the adapter validates and binds, NEVER mints daemon sessions. Module header documents: this gate is NON-authoritative pre-dispatch screening — authoritative per-command auth (proof-of-possession; design 718 'a valid stolen bearer without the client-key signature cannot authorize a command') stays daemon-side behind DispatchPort; parity across transports comes from both funneling into the SAME daemon check (design 1130). NO @moe/core dependency (layering: adapters depend on contracts; core is the pure-core layer — the verified dep graph has zero packages depending on @moe/core). Session registry: Map Mcp-Session-Id -> {server, transport, boundVerdict} — the SDK transport is ONE-SESSION-PER-INSTANCE (validateSession is strict equality against a single instance field), so multi-session requires this adapter-owned registry routing each request to its instance. Transport-level Mcp-Session-Id is minted by sessionIdGenerator (sync, SDK requirement) and bound to the daemon session inside the AWAITED onsessioninitialized (SDK awaits it before responding — verified webStandardStreamableHttp.js:530-536); onsessionclosed (DELETE) reaps registry + port.closeSession. Step-2 tests green.
implementationPlan.note: Reopen audit only: http-session.ts remains 224 lines, depends only on @moe/contracts, exposes the validate/bind/close-only port, revalidates per request, and maintains the adapter session registry. MCP typecheck passes; no production bytes changed.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/http/http-server.test.ts + src/http/http-server.ts. Build against WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport (fetch Request -> Promise<Response>; socket-free tests construct `new Request(...)` directly — the Node wrapper routes through @hono/node-server and is painful to mock; keep any node:http bridging as a thin outermost listener so tests exercise the same code prod uses). Wiring per request: (1) HOST/ORIGIN DEFENSE (BLOCKER from verification — SDK ships enableDnsRebindingProtection DEFAULT OFF): construct transports with enableDnsRebindingProtection: true + allowedHosts/allowedOrigins loopback-only defaults (127.0.0.1/localhost, configurable); tests: evil Origin header and wrong Host header -> refused with stable error, ZERO dispatch calls (design 1132/1139 loopback-only + strict Host/Origin); (2) BODY BOUND: the SDK has NO size limit (req.json() unguarded — verified) — adapter reads the body itself with a hard cap at MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES (1 MiB), tested at exactly N (accepted) and N+1 (stable refusal, zero dispatch), then hands the parsed value via the parsedBody option so the transport never re-reads; this same pre-read serves initialize detection; (3) AUTH BEFORE handleRequest: bearer check via http-session (there is NO auth hook inside the transport — wrap-before is the only mechanism and gives 'zero dispatch on auth failure' trivially); validated identity flows as authInfo (HandleRequestOptions.authInfo -> extra.authInfo); (4) CallTool handlers: same construction as stdio (shared generated schemas + name map imported from src/stdio/ — read-only import, no edits), thread extra.signal into port.dispatch*Bytes(bytes, signal); (5) parity fixture mode: enableJsonResponse: true (plain JSON body, cleanest byte-compare) + keepAliveMs: 0 (suppresses nondeterministic ': keepalive' frames); (6) DISCONNECT test asserts the VERIFIED SDK semantics: raw SSE disconnect does NOT abort extra.signal and does NOT stop dispatch — the stream unmaps, the handler completes, send() throws into onerror — so assert 'response never delivered + dispatch completed + nothing fabricated', NOT 'dispatch aborted'; explicit notifications/cancelled DOES abort the signal — separate test asserts the signal reaches the fake port; (7) DoD3 no-bypass: assert the HTTP ListTools set is EXACTLY the stdio generated set (import both, deep-equal) and no HTTP-only route exists (the adapter exposes exactly one MCP endpoint; registry rejects unknown session ids).

implementationPlan.description: src/http/http-resume.ts + resume tests inside http-server.test.ts (or a small http-resume.test.ts if cleaner — stay in owned paths). DECISION (verified, do not relitigate): resume is TYPED UNSUPPORTED in v1 — design 982 assigns the 'resumable cursor stream' to the CONTROL ROOM surface, not MCP; command-layer catch-up exists via events.read|wait with section-16.4 cursors. CRITICAL: omitting the SDK EventStore is NOT fail-closed by itself — verified webStandardStreamableHttp.js:238-244: without an eventStore the Last-Event-ID header is NEVER READ and the request silently gets a fresh SSE stream = a client that believes it resumed has a silent gap (fabricated continuity). Therefore http-resume.ts detects the Last-Event-ID header BEFORE transport.handleRequest and returns a typed stable refusal (registry-mapped error, MCP_RESUME_UNSUPPORTED reason in error.data; note: only a broken/hostile client can send it — without an EventStore no SSE event ever carries an id: field); NO EventStore is ever configured. Tests: GET and POST bearing Last-Event-ID -> stable refusal before the SDK sees the request, zero dispatch; normal GET (no header) -> standalone SSE stream works. Document the future path (implement SDK EventStore interface storeEvent/replayEventsAfter; SDK ships InMemoryEventStore under examples/) in a comment for the task that later lifts UNSUPPORTED.

2. The planning note rejected "HTTP-side port fork" as an *owned-paths violation*. That premise does not hold: packages/mcp/src/http/** is MY owned path, and the port is an INJECTED boundary — an adapter declaring the shape it needs from its injector is not a fork of stdio.
3. It is not a semantic fork either, because the widening is one-directional and compiler-checked. I declare in http-server.ts:
     dispatchCommandBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, signal?: AbortSignal): Uint8Array
   TypeScript parameter-arity assignability means every existing narrow port (StdioDispatchPort, ConformanceDispatchPort, and the shared createRecordingPort fake) is assignable to it. (3) Adapter-side authoritative auth / @moe/core dependency — REJECTED: layering (design 173; zero packages depend on @moe/core today); the adapter gate is NON-authoritative pre-dispatch screening; PoP/capability checks stay daemon-side behind DispatchPort — that sameness IS the design-1130 parity mechanism. planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Verified SDK 1.30.0 facts (file:line in workflow output): enableDnsRebindingProtection DEFAULTS OFF — Host/Origin checks run only when set (webStandardStreamableHttp.js:79,141-158); NO body size bound (req.json() unguarded) — parsedBody option lets the adapter pre-read with a cap; one transport instance = one session (validateSession strict equality; 400 missing header, 404 mismatch) — multi-session needs an adapter registry; NO auth hook — wrap-before-handleRequest, authInfo flows to extra.authInfo; raw SSE disconnect does NOT abort extra.signal (stream unmaps, handler completes, send() throws into onerror) — only notifications/cancelled aborts; sessionIdGenerator sync + onsessioninitialized/onsessionclosed AWAITED (js:530-536, 704-720); enableJsonResponse:true + keepAliveMs:0 give deterministic byte-compare fixtures; SSE frames as 'event: message
data: <json>

' (single data line — JSON.stringify never emits raw newlines); express NOT required (only @hono/node-server on the Node wrapper path; web-standard class avoids even that in tests). Design anchors: 1130 (capability-check parity), 1132/1139 (Host/Origin/CSRF, loopback defaults, credentials never in URLs/logs), 1141 (authenticated sessions + MCP authorization model), 987/761 (daemon session lifecycle + rotation revokes old credential), 718 (stolen bearer cannot authorize), 982 (resumable cursor stream = control room), 1135 (1 MiB body is the binding limit; subscriber/presence caps are daemon-side).
planningNotes.risks: (1) DNS-rebinding defense is the top security item: SDK default is OFF; forgetting enableDnsRebindingProtection + loopback allowlists ships an adapter that accepts evil-origin requests — step 4 makes it a constructor requirement with tests. (2) Silent resume gap: without the explicit Last-Event-ID refusal, clients believing they resumed have missing events — fabricated continuity; the SDK will not error for us. (3) Auth-verdict caching would break rotation revocation — per-request revalidation asserted by call-counting the fake port. (4) Dependency gate: stdio task may land without the signal param (comment-c638d1e8 is advisory) — step 1 blocks rather than forking the port from http/**. (5) Swapped cross-binding is adapter state — no daemon test covers it; the registry must bind verdict identity to Mcp-Session-Id and compare per request. (6) Disconnect-semantics test must assert what the SDK actually does (dispatch completes, response suppressed) — asserting 'dispatch aborted' would be red forever. (7) Shared tree: no stdio file edits (git status guard in step 7); attribute red repo gates to foreign in-flight work first.
